correctness.rationale: The signed truncated-power cube clipping formula holds for either sign of each nonzero normal coordinate by oriented one-coordinate integration. Every nontrivial strict Boolean threshold subset occurs on a nonempty open parameter chamber (perturbing zero normal entries). The rational branch N_J/(d! product eta_i) is distinct for every J: coefficients of squarefree monomials yield all weighted upper-set membership sums, whose Boolean-lattice Möbius inversion recovers J. An annihilating global polynomial therefore has T_d-2 distinct rational roots over R(eta,s); the explicit product of linear branch factors attains exactly this degree. Continuity covers degenerate normals, and the invertible affine substitution preserves the w-degree. Independently evaluated signed 2D clipping at normal (1,-1), threshold 1/4 gives exact area 23/32, verifying sign convention in one nontrivial case; the original standalone source also explicitly checks finite Boolean signatures, but finite checks cannot prove all d.
residual_risks: Possible unrecognized degeneracy under a novel equivalent definition of global polynomial relation; analyzed definition expressly excludes polynomial identically zero and fixes all hyperplane parameters. Published Boolean threshold counts, not finite witness-search, supply numerical examples.

value.rationale: The minimal global algebraic degree is an intrinsic sharp complexity measure for hyperplane cutoff volumes of a natural d-dimensional family. Identifying it with a familiar but fast-growing threshold-function count is structurally motivated and supplies both an explicit optimal annihilator and a nontrivial all-dimensional lower bound; not an arbitrary numeric table or mere clipping-formula restatement.
residual_risks: The polynomial is generally reducible; claim is explicitly w-degree and not a minimal irreducible polynomial.

limitations: Entire claim uses all generic and exceptional interior cuts; no statement about other convex polytopes, coefficient sizes, total polynomial degree, or irreducible minimal polynomial.
